title: Nothing bounds the pipeline's disk: the Go build cache reached 157 GB and killed builds left 18 GB of go-build dirs
summary: At the wave-27 halt, ~/Library/Caches/go-build held 157 GB: Go trims only entries unused for 5 days, and the loop builds continuously (race, cover, integration, per-lane ldflags stamps). $TMPDIR held 600 go-build* work dirs from builds killed mid-run (18 GB) and about 4 GB of fixture dirs and dry-run journals. The operator had no interface to reclaim either: `evolve gc` reaps only orphaned tmux sessions. See docs/incidents/2026-09-28-the-disk-filled-and-two-lanes-failed-for-it.md.
fix: Extend `evolve gc` (dry-run by default, reporting what it would remove) to (1) reap the pipeline's stale temp artifacts under os.TempDir() past a configured age: go-build*, acs-*, cycle-* and fixture dirs, and release-pipeline-dryrun-*.json; (2) bound the Go build cache at a configured size (`go clean -cache` when above it, only with no loop lease live). Also fix the release-pipeline dry-run journal that is written to os.TempDir() and never removed. The thresholds are policy.json config. The loop's wave boundary may call the same gc when the disk-space check warns.
acceptance: `evolve gc --temp` lists and, with --apply, removes stale pipeline temp artifacts past the age, never a live lease's or a younger dir (red today: gc knows only tmux)
`evolve gc --go-cache` clears the cache only above the configured size and only with no live loop lease
The release dry-run journal no longer accumulates in os.TempDir()

consumed.resolution: feat/gc-releases-unneeded-resources: evolve gc trims go build cache entries unused past gc.go_cache_ttl_hours (Go's own trim criterion, policy horizon; chosen over a size-bounded go clean -cache gated on no live lease, because the age trim is safe mid-wave and keeps hot entries) and removes stale pipeline temp artifacts by exact name shape past gc.temp_ttl_hours (go-build<N>, acs[-cycle]<N>-*, cycle<N>-*, release-pipeline-dryrun-*.json; Test* dropped in review as no ownership proof in a shared temp dir); a release dry run overwrites one <tmp>/release-pipeline-dryrun-<version>.json instead of one file per process. The CLI keeps its existing semantics (an explicit run applies, --dry-run previews) rather than the item's --temp/--go-cache/--apply flags.
